findings.title: Structurally valid cache corruption can remove a native working-text hold

evidence.mutation: complete_text false -> true in cached row only

findings.detail: Cache envelope validates current provider inventory, key and row shape, but never authenticates derived rows. An unchanged source provider with complete_text=false can be reconstructed from a changed cached row with complete_text=true, producing a cache hit and removing working_text_known_incomplete. This is material policy behavior, not just a display change.
findings.smallest_repair: Bind cached payload to an integrity digest and cache/parser implementation version; rebuild on mismatch. A checksum is an accidental-corruption control, not proof against a same-user adversarial rewrite of both data and checksum. Preserve genuine-index equivalence on new cache creation and test structurally valid mutation.
findings.scope: Synthetic native policy fixture; no canonical claim/source edited and no production incidence inferred.
